title: Can I SURVIVE Chaturanga?
summary: The creator plays Chaturanga (ancient Indian chess) online against higher-rated humans, aiming for three wins. Bishops are elephants that move exactly two squares diagonally and can jump; the queen is a counselor that moves one square diagonally; rooks are chariots (same as rooks); pawns move only one square (no double step, no en passant) and there is no castling. King and counselor start on swapped squares relative to modern chess. He wins four games.
rules: Elephant (bishop slot): moves exactly 2 squares diagonally, jumping over the intermediate square; can reach only 8 squares.
Chariot = rook; knight and king as normal.
Pawns move one square forward only (no double step, no en passant); capture diagonally; promote (to counselor, standard; inferred).
King and counselor positions are swapped compared with standard chess (per transcript).
win_condition: Checkmate. Goal: 3 wins vs higher-rated humans.
